chapters.title: Case
chapters.summary: Backend Engineer on a 16-person engineering team; 3-person health reporting group owning the report generation pipeline.
chapters.body: Ultrahuman builds metabolic and longevity hardware (including the Ring AIR and Blood Vision) trusted by over 5M+ users worldwide. Within a 16-person core engineering team, I worked in a 3-person health reporting group (a lead and two engineers) owning the AI report-generation pipeline for performance lab clients, alongside contributing to on-device Kotlin Multiplatform vital computation, a separate platform-wide app and website localization system, and a dynamic upsell engine evaluating user biometric cohorts for subscription extensions (Powerplugs).
points: Team & Scope: 16-person core engineering team; 3-person health reporting group (lead + 2 engineers) owning the end-to-end report generation pipeline.
Scale: Core platform serving 5M+ active users; clinical reporting pipeline processing multi-station diagnostics for performance lab clients.

Core Systems: AI health report-generation pipeline across 10+ stations, on-device KMP vital computation, separate platform-wide app & website localization system, and dynamic biometric upsell engine for subscription extensions (Powerplugs).

chapters.title: Problem
chapters.summary: Four distinct architectural bottlenecks spanning clinical reporting, edge vital latency, global app/website localization, and dynamic subscription upsells.

subsections.title: Fragmented Asynchronous Diagnostics & Doctor-in-the-Loop Validation
subsections.body: Health assessments span 10–15 disparate testing stations (DEXA, VO₂ max, blood biomarkers, gut microbiome). Results arrive asynchronously via APIs, PDFs, or delayed lab feeds arriving days later. Autonomous LLMs cannot be treated as final medical authority without qualified clinician review and granular section-level regeneration.
points: Heterogeneous inputs: REST APIs, PDF extracts, and asynchronous external laboratory feeds arriving days apart across 10+ stations.
Clinical accuracy & safety: LLM recommendations require doctor review and validation before reaching users.
Regeneration cost: Editing a single recommendation previously required manually re-running the entire 15-page document.

subsections.title: Cloud Batch Queue Latency & Network Dependency for Vital Scores
subsections.body: Ruby backend batch processing through job queues caused delayed vital calculations for ring wearers, introducing multi-second delays and failing when wearers lacked internet access.
points: High latency: Ring wearers woke up to delayed scores waiting for backend queue execution.
Network vulnerability: 0% offline execution; vitals could not be computed without cloud roundtrips.
Parity risk: Migrating vital calculations to device risked mathematical divergence from historical server baselines.

subsections.title: CJK Translation Nuance & Terminology Drift Across Global Apps & Web
subsections.body: A separate standalone translation workflow powered user-facing localization across the entire Ultrahuman mobile apps and website. Standard LLM translation failed on Chinese, Japanese, and Korean (CJK) due to context nuances, terminology drift, and trademark transliteration.
points: Context-dependent phrasing: CJK grammar requires deep domain context rather than verbatim literal translation.
Brand integrity: Lack of glossary constraints caused inconsistent transliteration of proprietary terms.
Repetitive overhead: Lack of prompt caching resulted in high token costs and latency on recurring system context.

subsections.title: Static Broadcast Promos & Resource-Intensive Platform-Wide Cohorting
subsections.body: Paid monthly subscription extensions ('Powerplugs' — e.g. cardio adaptability, deep health integrations) were previously recommended through static, one-size-fits-all in-app banners. Users received no contextual recommendations aligned with their dynamic physiological state (such as low sleep recovery or elevated resting heart rate). Concurrently, computing biomarker cohorts across millions of active platform users simultaneously risked severe database spikes and background queue starvation.
points: Low relevance & conversion: Static promotional broadcast banners failed to convert because recommendations were detached from user-specific biometric signals.
Platform-wide queue saturation: Evaluating cohort rules across 5M+ platform users in unthrottled bursts threatened core database and API latency.
Lack of temporal distribution: The architecture lacked a distributed batch evaluation pipeline to spread cohort assessments smoothly across 24-hour cycles.

chapters.title: Goal
chapters.summary: Target engineering objectives mapped directly to each of the four problem statements.

subsections.title: Dynamic Asynchronous Pipeline & Granular Clinician Regeneration
subsections.body: Build an asynchronous pipeline that dynamically triggers as prerequisite lab results arrive, producing 15-page reports with a doctor review loop allowing single-section regeneration.
points: Dynamic station DAG: Handle asynchronous data arrival without blocking or stalling reporting flows.
Human-in-the-loop: Generate → Review → Comment → Regenerate → Approve workflow for doctors.
Scoped section diffing: Regenerate only commented sections (e.g., diet plan) in seconds.

subsections.title: On-Device SpO₂ Computation with Strict Parity & ~80% Latency Cut
subsections.body: Port the SpO₂ algorithm to Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) for on-device execution, targeting an estimated ~80% latency reduction while achieving 99%+ numerical parity on wearer data.
points: Immediate local computation: Remove cloud batch processing dependency entirely.
100% offline execution: Enable users to compute recovery and vitals anywhere without connectivity.
Empirical validation: Prove 99%+ numerical parity across diverse device architectures with real ring wearer datasets.

subsections.title: High-Fidelity CJK App & Website Localization with Prompt Caching
subsections.body: Upgrade the platform-wide translation pipeline for CJK languages using curated domain glossaries, context injection, and prompt caching to boost quality from 86% to 91% and cut token costs by ~67%.
points: Glossary enforcement: Maintain exact trademark transliterations and medical terminology.
Context injection: Contextual analysis followed by nuanced script generation.
Prompt caching: Cut token costs by ~67% on recurring app and website translation prompts.

subsections.title: Nightly Biometric Cohort Evaluation & Distributed Daily Batch Queues
subsections.body: Revamp the dynamic upsell engine to evaluate users nightly against physiological conditions (heart rate variability, sleep scores, cardio recovery), queuing tailored Powerplug extension recommendations across distributed worker queues throughout the day in throttled batches to eliminate load spikes across 5M+ platform users.
points: Biometric cohort grouping: Automatically match users with relevant Powerplugs based on nightly physiological biomarkers and health scores.
Distributed worker queues: Spread cohort evaluation tasks across daily worker queues, executing in throttled batches to protect database performance.
Scalable conversion velocity: Deliver personalized, timely recommendations driving measurable subscription uptake without impacting core app APIs.

chapters.title: Approach
chapters.summary: Four dedicated architectural implementations addressing reporting, on-device execution, global platform localization, and subscription upsells.

subsections.title: Dynamic Report Generation Pipeline & Clinician-in-the-Loop Loop
subsections.body: Owned the end-to-end report generation pipeline within the 3-person reporting group. Built dynamic DAG compilation that triggers as prerequisite stations arrive, coupled with a clinician feedback loop that regenerates specific sections based on doctor comments without re-running the full document.
points: Dynamic Ingestion DAG: Reconciles REST APIs and extracted lab PDFs across 10+ stations into a unified biomarker schema.
Predefined Guidance Rules: Bound LLM reasoning to research-backed clinical rules and prompt constraints.
Targeted Section Regeneration: Doctors annotate specific blocks, triggering focused prompt regeneration that leaves the rest of the 15-page report intact.

subsections.title: Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) On-Device Computation Port
subsections.body: Contributed to shifting health computation from server background queues to on-device execution. Ported the SpO₂ algorithm from Ruby to Kotlin Multiplatform and validated numerical parity against real ring wearers.
points: Ruby to KMP Migration: Rewrote computation pipelines in shared Kotlin Multiplatform running natively on device.
Parity Test Suite: Built validation harness comparing server and device outputs against real ring wearer biometrics, proving 99%+ numerical parity.
Latency Benchmarks: Pre-release benchmarks by engineering leads projected an ~80% latency reduction by eliminating backend queues.

subsections.title: Separate Platform-Wide App & Website Localization Pipeline
subsections.body: Independent of health reporting, engineered a dedicated LLM translation flow powering user-facing localization across the entire Ultrahuman mobile applications and marketing web platform.
points: Curated Glossary Injection: Injected strict domain glossaries and trademark preservation rules for CJK scripts.
Context Injection: Enhanced translation quality from 86% to 91% for nuanced grammar and terminology.
Prompt Caching: Cached repetitive system instructions and contextual glossaries, slashing token costs by ~67%.

subsections.title: Biometric Upsell Engine Revamp for Subscription Extensions (Powerplugs)
subsections.body: Revamped the dynamic upsell engine recommending paid monthly subscription extensions ('Powerplugs' — e.g. cardio adaptability, deep health integrations). Evaluated biometric cohorts nightly (resting heart rate, sleep scores, recovery trends), spreading user evaluation across distributed worker queues throughout the day in throttled batches to prevent API or database spikes across 5M+ platform users.
points: Biometric Condition Cohorting: Evaluated users nightly based on physiological thresholds (heart rate, sleep quality, recovery metrics) to recommend relevant Powerplugs.
Distributed Batch Queuing: Spread evaluation jobs across daily worker queues, processing users in throttled batches to eliminate load spikes.
High-Velocity Monetization: Drove 8,000+ Powerplug subscription conversions within two months of deployment.

chapters.title: Learning
chapters.summary: Key technical takeaways on production LLM architecture, clinician-in-the-loop workflows, and edge computing.

takeaways.title: AI systems need structured workflows, not just prompts
takeaways.body: Production LLM applications are 90% ingestion, normalization, deterministic validation, and scoped regeneration rails. The model is merely one execution step in a resilient pipeline.

takeaways.title: Human review as a core product primitive
takeaways.body: In high-stakes health domains, total autonomy is an antipattern. Designing granular review, diffing, and single-section regeneration gives clinicians leverage without compromising medical accuracy.

takeaways.title: Architect for real-world asynchronous data
takeaways.body: Real-world medical data never arrives cleanly synchronized. Decoupling station dependencies prevents whole-system stalls when external lab feeds lag by days.

takeaways.title: Edge vs. cloud changes the interaction paradigm
takeaways.body: Migrating computation from background batch queues to on-device KMP isn't just an optimization; it transforms user experience from waiting for background jobs to instantaneous feedback.

chapters.title: Case
chapters.summary: Associate Software Engineer on the platform engineering team executing platform modernization, custom ORM development, and performance architecture.
chapters.body: Pencil is a B2B AI advertising platform used by large media agencies to manage advertising campaigns across Google Ads, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and LinkedIn. The platform allowed agencies to create advertisements, manage campaign workflows, and generate creative content variations—combining a Canva-like creative experience with AI-powered advertising workflows. As the platform grew, the volume of data stored and processed increased significantly. I worked as part of the platform engineering team on a coordinated platform modernization and performance initiative to evolve legacy patterns into an architecture that could scale with exponential business growth.
points: Team & Structure: Platform engineering team executing across development sprints, with engineers owning distinct functional domains.

My Primary Ownership: Custom ORM development, query-builder and data-access layer, schema/read optimizations, tenant metadata infrastructure, RBAC/permissions, and server-side Puppeteer PDF rendering.
Collaborative Delivery: Database migrations and planned downtime windows were coordinated with the lead engineer; changes were rolled out in controlled batches using feature flags.

Core Platform Objective: Evolve the architecture for data scale and throughput—replacing legacy patterns with Google Cloud SQL, custom ORM abstractions, multi-tenant metadata, and server-side rendering.

chapters.title: Problem
chapters.summary: Growing datasets bottlenecking database performance, rigid single schemas failing agency multi-tenancy, and client-side PDF rendering breaking layouts.

subsections.title: Growing Datasets, TypeORM Incompatibility & Join-Heavy Queries
subsections.body: Pencil's volume of campaign and creative data grew rapidly beyond the capacity of its original database design. The existing TypeORM-based access layer struggled with managed Google Cloud SQL requirements and lacked necessary low-level query capabilities. Furthermore, heavily normalized relational models forced application paths to execute expensive multi-table joins to assemble commonly accessed data, causing API response times to degrade under peak load.
points: Database strain: Rapidly expanding datasets degraded query performance across core campaign workflows.
ORM limitations: TypeORM wasn't working reliably with Cloud SQL and lacked required platform features.
Excessive joins: Strict normalization created expensive multi-join queries on hot read paths.

subsections.title: Rigid Global Schemas vs. Agency-Specific Workflow Requirements
subsections.body: Pencil served diverse advertising agencies, each with bespoke organizational structures, billing models, and workflow processes. A single monolithic database schema could not accommodate differing tenant requirements without constant hardcoded migrations or branching codebases. The platform needed a clean abstraction to let tenants define custom fields and business logic without code changes or database alterations.
points: Tenant variability: Agencies required custom fields and bespoke campaign attributes that differed wildly.
Schema friction: Adding columns globally for individual agency needs polluted schemas and slowed migrations.
Codebase sprawl: Risk of creating one-off code forks or brittle conditional logic per customer.

subsections.title: Client-Side react-to-pdf Inconsistencies & Font Latency
subsections.body: Pencil featured a rich-text copywriting editor where users created branded ad copy with custom fonts, colors, and styling. PDF exports were rendered in the client browser using react-to-pdf. This frequently broke: custom brand fonts had to be downloaded into the browser runtime prior to rendering, introducing severe export latency and causing layout mismatches, broken fonts, and discrepancies between editor and final output.
points: Visual fidelity degradation: react-to-pdf failed to consistently match the editor's styling and layout.
Font-loading penalties: Custom brand fonts had to be fetched and loaded client-side, stalling exports.
Unpredictable exports: Browser environment variations caused inconsistent document appearance.

chapters.title: Goal
chapters.summary: Modernize database infrastructure with custom ORM tooling, enable metadata-driven tenant customization, and move document rendering to the server.

subsections.title: Google Cloud SQL Infrastructure & Custom ORM Layer
subsections.body: Transition database layer to Google Cloud SQL to unlock managed partitioning, regional data distribution, and replication. Replace TypeORM with a custom query builder and ORM abstraction that natively enforces tenant isolation, handles data lifecycle rules (preventing hard deletes), and optimizes hot read paths over rigid normalization.
points: Managed infrastructure: Leverage Cloud SQL partitioning and replication instead of application-managed scaling.
Custom ORM abstraction: Build an expressive query builder supporting query chaining, tenant boundaries, and soft deletes across Node.js and Python.
Read-optimized schema: Restructure frequently queried tables to store related data together, cutting unnecessary joins.

subsections.title: Metadata-Driven Customization & Tenant Isolation
subsections.body: Architect a shared platform infrastructure where individual agency tenants configure bespoke fields, attributes, and workflows via dynamic metadata rather than schema alterations or code changes, accompanied by robust role-based access control (RBAC).
points: Metadata engine: Enable tenants to define custom fields and business logic on a unified core platform.
Clean tenant isolation: Guarantee strict data separation at the ORM and query level automatically.
Unified codebase: Maintain a single scalable deployment serving all enterprise agencies seamlessly.

subsections.title: Headless Server-Side PDF Pipeline with Visual Consistency
subsections.body: Replace client-side rendering with a server-side headless Puppeteer pipeline. Centralize font loading and layout calculation on the backend to achieve visual consistency with the copywriting editor and bring user-facing export times down to ~1.5 seconds.
points: Consistent rendering: Resolve dynamic brand font injection and cross-device margin drift by rendering in controlled server containers.
Server-side font caching: Preload and cache agency brand fonts to strip font-download latency from exports.
Sub-2s download speed: Target 65% faster rendering processing and ~1.5s total user-facing download speed.

chapters.summary: Custom ORM layer on Google Cloud SQL, dynamic metadata-driven tenant modeling, headless Puppeteer PDF workers, and phased feature flag rollouts.

subsections.title: Engineering a Custom Query Builder and Data-Access Layer
subsections.body: Designed and implemented a custom ORM abstraction supporting query building, fluent query chaining, and standard ORM operations across Node.js and Python. Embedded platform guardrails directly into the query abstraction: automatic tenant scoping, soft-delete enforcement, and optimized data serialization, freeing application developers from reinventing data access safety on every endpoint.
points: Fluent query chaining: Provided an intuitive, developer-friendly interface without TypeORM overhead.
Automated tenant filtering: Injected tenant boundary conditions into every query execution path.
Soft-delete lifecycle: Systematically safeguarded agency campaign records against destructive deletes.

subsections.title: Metadata-Driven Custom Fields, RBAC & Read Optimization
subsections.body: Engineered the platform-side metadata engine allowing agencies to define custom fields and attributes dynamically. Overhauled relational schemas to store frequently accessed campaign and creative metadata together—deliberately trading strict normalization for significant join reduction on high-traffic read paths. Implemented fine-grained multi-tenant RBAC with group/role hierarchy and composable boolean (AND/OR) permission checks across API endpoints.
points: Metadata-driven fields: Agencies configure custom fields without modifying underlying relational schemas.
Read-optimized schema: Reduced multi-table joins on hot queries, contributing to 30% faster API responses.
Enterprise RBAC: Unified permissions and access control directly into the data-access layer.

subsections.title: Puppeteer-Based Server-Side PDF Rendering Pipeline
subsections.body: Replaced browser-side react-to-pdf with headless Chromium via Puppeteer running on the server. Managed font lifecycles explicitly: preloading and caching custom agency brand fonts, standardizing CSS print media rules, and isolating document formatting in sandboxed workers. Delivered visual consistency with the editor while accelerating exports by 65%.
points: Consistent output: Resolved dynamic brand font injection and cross-device margin drift between editor and PDFs.
Server-side font lifecycle: Eliminated client font loading delays through server caching.
Fast export speeds: Slashed export latency by 30–40% and reached ~1.5s end-user download times.

subsections.title: Phased Feature-Flag Rollouts & Fastify Service Evolution
subsections.body: Modernized legacy Python-based API gateway patterns into a high-performance Node.js / Fastify service architecture. Collaborated across development sprints on schema migrations, coordinating planned downtime windows with the lead engineer and rolling out database and rendering changes progressively using tenant-level feature flags.
points: Service modernization: Shifted legacy gateway components to Node.js/Fastify microservices.
Planned downtime coordination: Participated in coordinated database migrations with batch rollouts.
Controlled feature flags: Progressively enabled new ORM and rendering paths per agency cohort.

chapters.title: Learning
chapters.summary: Key architectural principles on database modeling, abstraction boundaries, server-side control, and incremental modernization.

takeaways.title: Optimize for the workload, not theoretical purity
takeaways.body: The database redesign wasn't about textbook normalization. For frequently accessed campaign data, reducing expensive joins provided a significantly better real-world performance profile. The architecture was optimized around how Pencil actually accessed its data.

takeaways.title: Put infrastructure concerns behind abstractions
takeaways.body: Tenant isolation, soft-delete lifecycles, and database access shouldn't require every developer to remember a manual checklist of rules. By embedding platform-specific behaviors into the custom ORM, the platform guaranteed safer and more consistent access patterns by default.

takeaways.title: Server-side rendering provides deterministic control
takeaways.body: The PDF challenges demonstrated the hard limits of relying on client browsers for complex, branded documents. Moving rendering to server-side Puppeteer provided absolute control over fonts, layouts, and output consistency while dramatically improving speed.

takeaways.title: Modernization is incremental
takeaways.body: Large platforms cannot be replaced overnight. Modernization succeeded through domain-level sprints, schema refactoring, feature flags, and controlled batch migrations while the live product continued serving high-volume enterprise advertising campaigns.

Migrated document exports from client React rendering to server-side headless Puppeteer. Resolved dynamic brand font injection and cross-device margin drift, making output consistent and 65% faster (export download time ~1.5s, 30–40% latency reduction).

chapters.title: Case
chapters.summary: Associate Software Engineer in a 4-person engineering team with a technical lead at KeyValue Software Systems building Siren's AI-native layer.
chapters.body: Siren is a developer communication platform that helps engineering teams design and deliver notifications across email, SMS, push notifications, and chat. Working as part of a four-person engineering group with a technical lead, my focus was making Siren AI-native by exposing its communication capabilities to AI agents through a reusable Agent Toolkit and a standardized Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.
points: Team & Scope: 4-person engineering group with a technical lead owning the AI-agent integration layer.
Primary Ownership: Framework adoption, tool schema conversion, OpenAI/LangChain/CrewAI compatible tools, MCP tool implementations, agent integrations, documentation, and examples.
Collaborative Delivery: Automated packaging and CI/CD publishing workflows were established by another team engineer.
Core Objective: Let developers instruct AI agents on what they want to communicate via natural language intent, rather than writing boilerplate integration code for every notification channel.

chapters.title: Problem
chapters.summary: Three distinct engineering challenges: rigid imperative SDK wiring, fragmented agent framework interfaces, and rapidly shifting ecosystem specifications.

subsections.title: Rigid API/SDK Wiring vs. Intent-Driven Communication
subsections.body: Traditional notification integrations forced developers to write imperative boilerplate (Application → SDK → Notification API → Email/SMS/Push), manually selecting operations, constructing request payloads, and writing routing logic. As AI agents emerged, developers needed an intent-based model where an agent could execute high-level instructions ('Send an email to the new user welcoming them') without bespoke code for each trigger.
points: Imperative integration friction: Developers spent hours writing plumbing code for standard notification triggers.
Lack of semantic understanding: APIs could not interpret natural language instructions directly.
High barrier for AI agents: Existing endpoints lacked schemas that LLMs could reason about or call safely.

subsections.title: Incompatible Tool Conventions Across Agent Ecosystems
subsections.body: Different agent frameworks (OpenAI Function Calling, LangChain, CrewAI) expected tools and schemas to be defined, validated, and executed with completely different signatures and parameter structures. Forcing developers to hand-roll custom adapters for every Siren operation in each framework created severe integration fragmentation.
points: Schema incompatibility: OpenAI JSON schemas, LangChain StructuredTools, and CrewAI tools require divergent formats.
Dual-language barrier: Enterprise stacks required idiomatic tooling across both TypeScript/Node.js and Python ecosystems.
Maintenance overhead: Supporting multiple frameworks without a shared core layer led to duplicated logic and brittle glue code.

subsections.title: Building Against Rapidly Evolving Specifications & Standards
subsections.body: AI agent tooling and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) were in their earliest releases when development began. Upstream specifications, client conventions, and library APIs were shifting continuously without established industry best practices, making stability and future-proof design a strict engineering constraint.
points: Unstable upstream APIs: Framework tool interfaces and protocol drafts underwent frequent breaking changes.
Absence of battle-tested patterns: Integration conventions had to be architected from scratch through empirical testing against agent workflows.
Compatibility pressure: Integrations had to remain reliable for developers while the underlying standards were actively maturing.

chapters.title: Goal
chapters.summary: Target engineering objectives mapped directly to developer experience, cross-framework compatibility, and resilient MCP standardization.

subsections.title: Natural Language Intent as the Integration Layer
subsections.body: Shift Siren's primary interaction model from purely API-oriented to intent-oriented, enabling agents to parse natural-language instructions, determine the correct notification operation, and construct payloads while preserving developer control over explicit templates.
points: Intent resolution: Enable agents to trigger complex notifications from simple prompt instructions.
Preserve developer control: Allow explicit templates, content overrides, and parameter constraints when needed.
Effort reduction: Cut developer integration effort by ~75% (zero-install MCP server setup vs. manual SDK integration to wire notifications and emails).

subsections.title: Unified Agent Toolkit & Native Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server
subsections.body: Build a single reusable abstraction layer over Siren's capabilities and expose it via both a cross-framework Agent Toolkit (TypeScript & Python) and a standalone MCP server executable via npx.
points: Framework agnostic: Native compatibility with OpenAI, LangChain, CrewAI, and custom agent swarms.
Standard protocol: Support standardized tool discovery and invocation via the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Dual-language SDKs: Provide idiomatic @trysiren/agent-toolkit (npm) and siren-agent-toolkit (PyPI) packages.

subsections.title: Resilient Adapter Architecture for Rapidly Shifting Specs
subsections.body: Design clean decoupled boundaries between internal Siren operations and external agent frameworks, insulating application developers from upstream protocol churn and specification updates.
points: Decoupled tool schemas: Isolate core platform capabilities from framework-specific serialization formats.
Continuous compatibility: Maintain stable developer DX across iterative agent framework releases.
Self-documenting interfaces: Provide comprehensive documentation, quickstarts, and sample agent workflows.

chapters.title: Approach
chapters.summary: Architecture bridging existing Siren platform capabilities with agent frameworks and MCP servers through reusable tool schemas.

subsections.title: Tool Schema Conversion & Multi-Framework Agent Toolkit
subsections.body: Mapped Siren's existing platform operations (messaging, templates, users, workflows) into structured agent-callable tools. Built a unified core abstraction that dynamically converts schemas into framework-specific signatures for OpenAI Function Calling, LangChain StructuredTools, and CrewAI across TypeScript (@trysiren/agent-toolkit) and Python (siren-agent-toolkit).
points: Semantic tool definitions: Authored descriptive schemas and parameters so LLMs understand tool purpose reliably.
Multi-framework adapters: Provided drop-in compatibility across OpenAI, LangChain, and CrewAI without vendor lock-in.
Dual-stack distribution: Maintained parity across TypeScript/Node.js and Python implementations.

subsections.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server Implementation
subsections.body: Architected a dedicated MCP server package (@trysiren/mcp) implementing the standardized Model Context Protocol over JSON-RPC. Allows Claude desktop, cursor agents, and external agent runtimes to dynamically discover and invoke Siren tools directly via npx (@trysiren/mcp) without custom integration code.
points: Standard tool discovery: Exposed Siren communication tools through the universal MCP specification.
Zero-install execution: Supported direct execution via npx -y @trysiren/mcp for frictionless local and server workflows.
Granular capability exposure: Enabled agents to inspect available templates and send single or batch dispatches safely.

subsections.title: Decoupled Adapter Boundaries Under Changing Standards
subsections.body: Treated rapid ecosystem evolution as a core engineering constraint. Designed clear abstraction barriers between raw Siren REST endpoints and external agent schemas, allowing our team to absorb upstream specification changes (such as MCP draft updates and framework method renames) without breaking end-developer applications.
points: Defensive abstraction layers: Shielded application developers from frequent upstream API and spec shifts.
Empirical agent validation: Tested tool invocations against live agent runs to detect prompt regression early.
Ecosystem adaptability: Kept public integration patterns stable even as underlying packages evolved.

subsections.title: Public Documentation, Examples & Technical Strategy
subsections.body: Co-authored public technical documentation, implementation quickstarts, and architectural guides on how to make existing B2B products AI-native. Documented integration patterns for multi-agent swarms (CrewAI) and autonomous workflows.
points: Official documentation: Authored comprehensive setup guides for Agent Toolkit and MCP server.
Real-world examples: Built end-to-end agent workflow demos for welcome emails and transactional alerts.
Technical strategy publication: Published technical article on KeyValue's engineering blog regarding AI-native product transitions.

chapters.title: Outcome
chapters.summary: ~75% reduction in developer setup effort, native support for major agent frameworks, and public distribution on npm and PyPI.

table.impact: ~75% reduction (zero-install MCP setup vs. manual SDK integration to wire notifications and emails)
Native support for OpenAI, LangChain, CrewAI & MCP
Reusable Agent Toolkit + Standalone MCP Server
Dual-stack TypeScript/Node.js (npm) & Python (PyPI)
Global npm package executable via npx (@trysiren/mcp)
~100 peak registry downloads across npm and PyPI
Transitioned from imperative API wiring to natural-language intent

chapters.title: Learning
chapters.summary: Key technical lessons on making existing platforms AI-native, tool schema engineering, and early-ecosystem adaptability.

takeaways.title: AI-native doesn't mean rebuilding the product
takeaways.body: Siren already had robust notification delivery capabilities. The challenge was building an agent-facing discovery and execution layer over existing capabilities rather than duplicating underlying infrastructure.

takeaways.title: Tool design matters as much as model quality
takeaways.body: An AI agent can only reliably use a capability if the tool interface is understandable. Designing explicit schemas, clear parameter constraints, and intuitive descriptions is critical for reliable agent execution.

takeaways.title: Early ecosystems require adaptability as an architecture feature
takeaways.body: Working with rapidly evolving agent frameworks and MCP specifications meant engineering wasn't simply following established documentation. Decoupled adapter layers allowed us to maintain a stable developer experience while the underlying ecosystem matured.

bullets: Designed and built core communication rails and message protocols powering multi-agent orchestration between autonomous AI agents.

Built the Siren Agent Toolkit adhering to OpenAI tool specs for LangChain/CrewAI, and engineered a standalone Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that reduced developer setup effort by ~75% (zero-install MCP setup vs. manual SDK integration).
Published open-source packages to npm (@trysiren/agent-toolkit, @trysiren/mcp) and PyPI (siren-agent-toolkit), achieving ~100 peak registry downloads across ecosystems.
Co-authored official public documentation, code examples, and technical article on transitioning products to AI-native.

faqs: Do you both design and build websites?
Yes. I handle the whole thing, design and development, with one set of hands. My experience spans full-stack products, backend platforms, and the interfaces that connect people to them.
Where are you based, and do you work remotely?
I'm based in Kerala, India (open to relocate and remote) and work with teams across the world.
What technologies do you build with?
I work mostly with Node.js, TypeScript, Python, Ruby on Rails, React, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS, and MCP. I choose the tools around the problem rather than forcing every product into one stack.
Can you build an online store or e-commerce site?
Yes. I've built service architectures and inventory and order-processing workflows for e-commerce products, with a focus on reliable backend systems and integrations.
How much does a website cost?

It depends entirely on what you need. I work across a wide range of budgets, from smaller sites through to large, complex builds. Tell me what you have in mind and I'll scope it and give you a clear, fixed quote.
How long does a project take?
Most sites take from a few weeks to a couple of months, depending on scope, content readiness and how many rounds of feedback we go through. I'll give you a realistic timeline up front.
Can you redesign or rebuild my existing website?

Yes. A lot of my work is refreshing tired sites that no longer reflect the quality of the business, including migrations from older WordPress builds, with care taken to keep your SEO and rankings intact.
Do you offer ongoing support after launch?
Yes. I offer ongoing support and retainer agreements to keep your site updated, secure and performing after launch and as your business scales.
